l: The Fort Worth Police Department through the mediation process, seeks to enhance communications between and restore the interests of the involved parties while also addressing the community member's complaint against the officer in a timely, fair, and equitable manner.

A. Ineligible Issue - An issue is ineligible for the mediation process if it can be described as a significant policy violation or if it is so egregious that it threatens the integrity of the Fort Worth Police Department (e.g., deadly force or civil rights violations). An issue may be ineligible for mediation if the nature or magnitude of the issue makes it impractical for mediation. Certain management decisions, discipline, or policy issues shall not be eligible for mediation.
B. Involved Parties - The phrase used to describe collectively the complainant and officer.
C. Mediation - A forum in which an impartial person, the mediator, facilitates communication between parties to promote understanding and reconciliation that may result in a resolution.
D. Mediation Procedure - The term used to describe all mediation-related activities collectively, including intake, education, interviews, mediation sessions, evaluations, and file closure.
E. Mediation Session - The mediation meeting wherein the parties and the mediator assemble in private to discuss issues of concern.

F. Mediator - An individual who has completed a minimum of forty-five (45) hours of mediation training and is selected to act as a neutral participant during a mediation session to facilitate the discussion.
G. Participant - Any party who has a role in the mediation procedure including any interview, training, or meeting.
H. Party - Any person having an interest in an issue or concern forwarded to the Office of Police Oversight Monitor (OPOM) or Fort Worth Police Department for mediation.

I. Support Person - The complainant and the Fort Worth Police Department member may each bring an individual as a Support Person to the mediation. This individual will not participate in the mediation except to observe and provide support. If that individual is an adult accompanying a minor, or was present at the time of the if the incident, they may participate in the mediation.

A. When a complaint is received by the Office of Police Oversight Monitor (OPOM) or the Fort Worth Police Department, Internal Affairs will assess whether the officer is eligible to participate in the mediation procedure. If eligible and the complainant is determined to be eligible by OPOM and the complainant agrees, an offer to mediate will be extended to the officer.
1. The officer may not be eligible to participate in mediation if:
a. The officer has displayed a similar pattern of the accused behavior within the past year, or
b. The officer has participated in mediation more than three (3) times that year.

2. OPOM and Internal Affairs shall review referred complaints to ensure that they are eligible for mediation. C. After determination of eligibility and their agreement, OPOM will contact the involved parties to begin the mediation procedure.

1. Officers shall cooperate with OPOM personnel in scheduling mediation meetings and throughout the mediation process. Officers who fail to adhere to these requirements will have their complaint returned to Internal Affairs to facilitate the normal investigative process.
a. If the involved officer is going to be late for the scheduled mediation, they should contact the OPOM immediately to inform them what time they will arrive.

b. If the involved officer is unable to attend the mediation due to an unforeseen emergency, they should make every reasonable effort to immediately notify OPOM in order to reschedule the session. The OPOM will contact Internal Affairs to determine if there was a legitimate reason for the officer’s failure to attend the mediation session.
c. Unless extenuating circumstances, if the officer fails to attend, the complaint will be fully investigated by Internal Affairs.
2. Officers shall wear their city-issued uniform or professional business attire for the scheduled mediation session.

D. A mediator will be chosen from a random pool of volunteer mediators. Unless there are extenuating circumstances, mediation shall occur within thirty (30) calendar days of acceptance by the parties and selection of a mediator.
E. If the involved parties decline to participate in the mediation process at any time, then the case will be resolved through the standard investigative process.

F. Complaints eligible for resolution through mediation shall be processed and completed within forty-five (45) calendar days from the date the complaint was approved for the mediation procedure unless extenuating circumstances.

G. All proceedings in the course of mediation shall remain confidential. No employee or officer may disclose any confidential information related to the involved parties’ mediation procedure or session or engage in any investigative or prosecuting function arising out of a complaint in which such person has acted on behalf of the agency.

H. The mediation procedure is not punitive and involved parties shall not be penalized or disciplined for participating. However, mediation cannot shield officers from an investigation of a violation of the law, for any allegation not mediated, or for any allegation not eligible to be resolved by the mediation process.

I. Any violation of the confidentiality laws, regulations and policies, or act of retaliation related to mediation shall be investigated according to City of Fort Worth and/or Fort Worth Police Department regulations, and employees and officers may be subject to disciplinary action.
A. Both parties are required to participate in good faith in the mediation session. Agreements are totally voluntary, but not required, and when applicable, must be agreed to by both parties.
B. Failure to reach an agreement has no impact on any later consideration of the complaint.
C. Issues addressed by reconciliation using the mediation process are closed and noted as “Mediated.”
